meta.title: SecHeaders Lab — passive website security review
meta.description: Grade a website’s HTTP security headers, TLS, cookies and information disclosure from A+ to F, with copy-ready fixes for Nginx, Apache, IIS, Next.js, Netlify and Cloudflare.

footer.disclaimer: SecHeaders Lab only reads what a site already sends to every visitor. It is not a penetration test, and its results are for guidance. Only scan sites you are authorized to assess.
footer.privacy: No accounts, no tracking, and scan results are never saved.
footer.author: Built by Mohammed Alrabai

home.title: Grade your website’s security headers in seconds
home.lead: Check your site’s HTTP security headers, HTTPS setup, cookies and information leaks. Get a grade from A+ to F and ready-to-copy fixes for your server.

HDR-HSTS.title: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
HDR-HSTS.why: HSTS tells browsers to use only HTTPS for your site for a set time, even when someone types or follows an http:// link. After the first secure visit, this protects visitors from downgrade and cookie-theft attacks on networks an attacker controls.

states.notHttps: The final page is served over plain HTTP, so HSTS cannot take effect.
states.invalidMaxAge: The header has no valid max-age (or max-age is 0), so it has no effect.
states.short: max-age is {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}; at least 180 days is recommended, ideally one year or more.
states.noSubdomains: Enabled for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, but without includeSubDomains, so subdomains are not covered.
states.belowOneYear: Enabled for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} with includeSubDomains. One year or more is needed for A+.
states.ok: Enabled for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, including subdomains.

HDR-CSP.title: Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
HDR-CSP.why: A CSP limits where scripts and other resources may load from. A strict policy is one of the strongest browser defenses against cross-site scripting (XSS).

states.missing: No enforced Content-Security-Policy header was found.
states.reportOnlyIgnored: Only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only is present; it reports violations but blocks nothing.
states.weak: A policy is enforced but has weaknesses.
states.noScriptControl: Neither script-src nor default-src is set, so scripts are not restricted (−10).
states.unsafeInline: 'unsafe-inline' allows inline scripts without a nonce or hash (−10).
states.unsafeEval: 'unsafe-eval' allows eval() and similar string-to-code functions (−5).
states.broadSource: Scripts may load from any host or scheme (*, http:, https: or data:) (−5).
states.objectSrc: object-src is not 'none', so plugins and embedded objects are allowed (−3).
states.noBaseUri: base-uri is not set; base-uri 'none' or 'self' stops injected base elements from redirecting relative URLs.

HDR-FRAME.title: Clickjacking protection (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
HDR-FRAME.why: Without it, other sites can load your pages in a hidden frame and trick users into clicking things they cannot see (clickjacking).

states.missing: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors restricts framing.
states.allowFrom: X-Frame-Options ALLOW-FROM is obsolete and ignored by modern browsers.

HDR-XCTO.title: X-Content-Type-Options
HDR-XCTO.why: The nosniff value stops browsers from guessing a file’s type, which could otherwise turn an uploaded text file into script or style.

HDR-REFERRER.title: Referrer-Policy
HDR-REFERRER.why: Controls how much of the page address is sent to other sites when people follow links. Full URLs can leak tokens, IDs or private paths.

states.missing: Not set; the browser default applies.
states.invalid: No valid policy value was recognized; the browser default applies.
states.leaky: {policy} sends the full URL to other sites.
states.ok: The policy {policy} limits what is shared.

HDR-PERMISSIONS.title: Permissions-Policy
HDR-PERMISSIONS.why: Turns off powerful browser features you do not use, such as camera, microphone and geolocation, so injected or third-party code cannot use them.

HDR-COOP.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP)
HDR-COOP.why: The same-origin value isolates your window from pages it opens and from the page that opened it, which reduces cross-window attacks and side-channel leaks.

HDR-XXSS.title: X-XSS-Protection
HDR-XXSS.why: The old browser XSS filter has been removed from modern browsers and could itself cause problems. Rely on CSP, and send 0 or nothing.

states.enabled: The legacy XSS filter is enabled (informational).
states.absent: Not set, which is fine for modern browsers.

HDR-DUPLICATE.title: Duplicate headers
HDR-DUPLICATE.why: When a header is sent twice, browsers may use either value or combine them, so the effective policy becomes unclear.

states.found: Sent more than once: {headers}. The first value was evaluated.

TLS-AVAILABLE.title: HTTPS availability
TLS-AVAILABLE.why: Without HTTPS, anyone on the network path can read and change everything sent between visitors and your site.

states.unavailable: No TLS connection could be made on port 443.

TLS-CERT-VALID.title: Certificate validity
TLS-CERT-VALID.why: Browsers show a full-page warning for invalid certificates, and visitors who click through are exposed to interception.

states.ok: The certificate is trusted and matches the host name.
states.notYetValid: The certificate is not valid yet.
states.hostnameMismatch: The certificate does not cover this host name.
states.untrusted: The certificate is not issued by a trusted authority (for example, it is self-signed).
states.notEvaluated: Could not be checked because HTTPS is not available.

TLS-CERT-EXPIRY.title: Certificate expiry
TLS-CERT-EXPIRY.why: When a certificate expires, browsers block the site with a full-page warning. Automated renewal prevents this.

states.soon: Expires in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}; renew it now.
states.month: Expires in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}; make sure renewal is automated.
states.ok: Expires in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.

TLS-PROTOCOL.title: TLS protocol version
TLS-PROTOCOL.why: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known weaknesses and are deprecated. Modern clients use TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

states.old: The server negotiated {protocol}, which is deprecated.

TLS-HTTP-REDIRECT.title: HTTP to HTTPS redirect
TLS-HTTP-REDIRECT.why: Visitors who type the address without https:// should be sent straight to the secure site; otherwise their first request travels unencrypted.

states.ok: http:// redirects to HTTPS on the same site.
states.noRedirect: http:// does not redirect to HTTPS.
states.otherSite: http:// redirects to HTTPS on a different site.
states.httpUnavailable: Port 80 is not reachable; the site is served over HTTPS only, which is fine.

CK-SECURE.title: Cookie Secure attribute
CK-SECURE.why: Secure cookies are only sent over HTTPS, so they cannot leak over an unencrypted connection.

states.noCookies: No cookies are set on this page.
states.violations: {count, plural, one {# cookie lacks} other {# cookies lack}} Secure: {cookies}.
states.notHttps: Not applicable: the page is served over HTTP.

CK-HTTPONLY.title: Cookie HttpOnly attribute
CK-HTTPONLY.why: HttpOnly hides cookies from JavaScript, so a cross-site scripting bug cannot read session cookies.

states.noCookies: No cookies are set on this page.
states.violations: {count, plural, one {# cookie lacks} other {# cookies lack}} HttpOnly: {cookies}.

CK-SAMESITE.title: Cookie SameSite attribute
CK-SAMESITE.why: SameSite limits when cookies are sent with requests started by other sites, which mitigates cross-site request forgery (CSRF).

states.noCookies: No cookies are set on this page.
states.ok: All cookies set a valid SameSite value.
states.violations: {count, plural, one {# cookie has} other {# cookies have}} no valid SameSite value: {cookies}.

CK-PREFIX.title: Cookie name prefixes
CK-PREFIX.why: The __Host- and __Secure- prefixes make browsers reject a cookie unless it is set with the required secure attributes.

states.noCookies: No cookies are set on this page.
states.ok: Cookie prefixes are used correctly, or not used.
states.violations: {count, plural, one {# cookie breaks its} other {# cookies break their}} prefix rules: {cookies}.

INF-SERVER.title: Server header
INF-SERVER.why: A version number helps attackers match your server to known vulnerabilities.

states.version: The Server header reveals a version number.
states.present: The Server header names the software but not its version.

INF-POWERED-BY.title: X-Powered-By header
INF-POWERED-BY.why: It reveals the framework or language behind the site, which helps attackers target known issues.

INF-ASPNET.title: ASP.NET version headers
INF-ASPNET.why: X-AspNet-Version and X-AspNetMvc-Version reveal exact framework versions.

states.present: An ASP.NET version header is sent.

steps.certificate: Install a certificate from a trusted certificate authority that covers every host name of the site, serve the full chain, and automate renewal with an ACME client.
steps.hostManagedTls: TLS versions are managed by your hosting platform. Check its TLS settings and keep only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 enabled.
steps.iisTls: On Windows Server, disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in the Schannel protocol settings (registry or Group Policy), keep TLS 1.2 and 1.3 enabled, then restart the server.
steps.hostManagedRedirect: Your hosting platform terminates HTTPS. Turn on its “force HTTPS” or HTTPS-redirect option for this site.
steps.hostServerHeader: The Server header is set by your hosting platform and usually cannot be changed. Make sure it does not include a version number.
steps.removeInApp: Remove the {name} header where it is added: in the application or framework settings, or in a reverse proxy in front of it.
steps.aspnetOnly: Only ASP.NET sends this header. Turn it off in web.config (see the IIS tab) or in your ASP.NET application.
steps.cookieInApp: Set the Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes where the application creates the cookie, usually in the framework’s session or cookie settings.
steps.cookiePrefix: Rename the cookie with the __Host- prefix and set it with Secure, Path=/ and no Domain attribute, or use __Secure- with Secure.
steps.duplicateHeaders: Send each security header once. Remove the duplicate from either the application or the server or CDN configuration.
steps.cloudflareHeader: In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to Rules → Overview, create a Response Header Transform Rule, and use “Set static” to set {name} to: {value}
steps.cloudflareHsts: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates, enable HSTS, set Max Age to at least 12 months and turn on “Apply HSTS policy to subdomains”.
steps.cloudflareRemoveHeader: In the Cloudflare dashboard, create a Response Header Transform Rule that uses “Remove” for {name}, or remove it at your origin server.
steps.cloudflareServer: Cloudflare Transform Rules cannot change the Server header. Remove version information at your origin server.
steps.cloudflareAlwaysHttps: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates and turn on Always Use HTTPS (the encryption mode must not be Off).
steps.cloudflareMinTls: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates and set Minimum TLS Version to 1.2 or higher.
steps.cloudflareCertificate: In the Cloudflare dashboard, choose the Full (strict) encryption mode on the SSL/TLS Overview page, check that Edge Certificates shows an active certificate, and install a valid certificate on your origin.

about.title: Methodology
about.intro: How SecHeaders Lab inspects a site, which checks it runs, how the score and grade are calculated, and what it does not do.

what.title: What a scan does
what.fetch: One normal GET request for the address you enter, following at most five redirects. Every redirect target is checked again before it is followed.
what.tls: One TLS handshake on port 443 to read the certificate and the negotiated protocol. No application data is sent on it.
what.redirect: One request to http:// on the same host to see whether it redirects to HTTPS.
what.never: Nothing else: no crawling, no path guessing and no attack payloads. Only public addresses on ports 80 and 443 are contacted.

checks.title: Checks and weights
checks.intro: Each failed or weak check deducts points from 100. Informational findings never deduct points.

grading.title: Score and grade
grading.formula: Score = 100 minus all deductions, never below 0. The grade follows the score:
grading.aPlus: A+ also requires no failed checks, HSTS for at least one year, and a strict Content-Security-Policy. Otherwise a score of 95 or more is an A.

limits.title: Limitations
limits.passive: The scan is passive. It reports what a site sends to every visitor; it cannot find vulnerabilities in the application itself.
limits.single: Only the page at the address you enter (after redirects) is inspected. Other pages, and visitors in other regions or behind other CDN nodes, may receive different headers.
limits.meta: Policies set with HTML meta tags are not read, because the page body is never read.
limits.compliance: Results are informational and are not a penetration test or a compliance assessment.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: There are no accounts, no analytics and no tracking, and scan results are never stored. The only cookie is an optional theme preference.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.body: Only scan sites that you own or are authorized to assess. The service is provided as is, without warranty, and its results must not be relied on as a security certification.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How SecHeaders Lab handles information: no accounts, no analytics, no tracking and no stored scans.
privacy.intro: SecHeaders Lab is designed to work with as little information as possible. This policy explains exactly what happens to your data when you use the site.

sections.title: Who runs this site
paragraphs: SecHeaders Lab is an independent, open-source project built and maintained by Mohammed Alrabai. It is not operated by a company and has no commercial purpose.

sections.title: What we do not collect
items: No analytics, advertising, fingerprinting or tracking of any kind.
No third-party scripts, fonts or embedded content. Every file is served from this site.
No stored scan results, and no record of full addresses: the scan log keeps only the host name.

sections.title: What happens when you run a scan
paragraphs: The address you enter is sent to our server. The server makes one ordinary request to that site, reads its TLS certificate and checks whether HTTP redirects to HTTPS. The result is returned to your browser and is not saved.

To operate and protect the service, the server writes one short log entry per scan. It contains only the time, the outcome, the duration, the scanned host name and the number of findings. It never includes the path or query string of the address, and the application does not record your IP address.

sections.title: What the scanned site sees
paragraphs: The request reaches the scanned site from our server, not from your browser. The site sees our server’s address and a user agent that names SecHeaders Lab and links to the methodology page. It receives no information about you, including your IP address.

sections.title: Hosting
paragraphs: The site is hosted by Netlify. To deliver pages, enforce rate limits and protect the service from abuse, Netlify processes technical data such as IP addresses and request details under its own privacy terms.

sections.title: Shared result links
paragraphs: The scanned address is part of the result page’s link, so it is kept in your browser history and is visible to anyone you share the link with.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: The site stores two small preferences in your browser: an optional cookie for your theme, and a local storage entry recording that you closed the cookie notice. The Cookie Policy describes both in detail.

sections.title: Your choices
paragraphs: Because the application keeps no personal data about you, there is no profile to view, export or delete. You can remove both stored preferences at any time from your browser settings.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: Any change will be published on this page with a new date. The complete history of changes is public in the project’s repository.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.description: The rules for using SecHeaders Lab: scan only sites you are authorized to assess, and treat results as guidance.
terms.intro: By using SecHeaders Lab, you agree to these terms. Please read them before running a scan.

sections.title: The service
paragraphs: SecHeaders Lab performs a passive, read-only review of what a public website already sends to every visitor: its HTTP security headers, TLS certificate and protocol, cookies and information-disclosure headers. It returns a score, a grade and suggested fixes.
The service is free, requires no account, and may change or become unavailable at any time.

sections.title: Acceptable use
items: Scan only websites that you own or are authorized to assess.
Do not use the service to target internal or private networks, or to harass, overload or disrupt any website.
Do not attempt to bypass the rate limit (currently 10 scans per minute), the address restrictions or any other security control.
Do not run automated, high-volume scans. If you need them, run the open-source code on your own infrastructure.

sections.title: Results are guidance, not certification
paragraphs: A scan is not a penetration test, a vulnerability assessment or a compliance certification. It inspects only the response for the address you enter; other pages, regions or CDN locations may behave differently.
Use the results as guidance, and test every change in your own environment before relying on it.

sections.title: No warranty
paragraphs: The service and its results are provided “as is” and “as available”, without warranties of any kind, including accuracy, availability or fitness for a particular purpose. To the extent permitted by law, the author is not liable for any loss or damage arising from the use of the service or its results.

sections.title: Open-source license
paragraphs: The source code is published under the MIT License. These terms apply to the hosted service; the license governs your use of the code.

sections.title: Security research
paragraphs: If you find a vulnerability in SecHeaders Lab, report it privately as described in the project’s security policy. Do not exploit it, and never use it against websites you do not own.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: These terms may be updated. The current version is always published on this page with its date.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.description: The only data SecHeaders Lab stores in your browser: an optional theme cookie and a notice preference. No tracking cookies.
cookies.intro: SecHeaders Lab uses no tracking, analytics or advertising cookies. This page lists exactly what the site stores in your browser, and why.

sections.title: What cookies are
paragraphs: Cookies are small pieces of text that a website asks your browser to store. Local storage is a similar browser feature that keeps small values on your device.

sections.title: What we do not use
items: No advertising, marketing or social media cookies.
No third-party cookies. Our server never sets cookies, and no external services are loaded.

sections.title: Your choices
paragraphs: Both items are optional preferences that only change how the site looks and behaves for you. The site works fully without them.
You can delete them at any time from your browser settings, or block cookies for this site. The theme will then follow your system setting.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: Any change will be published on this page with a new date. The complete history of changes is public in the project’s repository.
